ds: Disguising proceeds of crime and moving value through trade transactions by manipulating invoicing, quantity, quality or description of goods and services. Techniques include over- and under-invoicing, multiple invoicing, phantom shipments and use of unrelated third parties.

src.t: FATF and Egmont Group, Trade-Based Money Laundering: Trends and Developments (2020)
ICC, BAFT and Wolfsberg Group, Trade Finance Principles (2019 update)

rat: Invoice manipulation and LC/bill of lading discrepancies in trade finance.

ind.n: Invoice price significantly differs from market value
ind.cx: Unit prices are well above or below the normal market range for the goods without a commercial rationale.
ind.fp: Discounts, grade differences, and volatile commodities can explain variance.
ind.ds: Price paid differs sharply from market value, comparable sales or estimates without commercial justification.
ind.cn: Transaction price materially different from market value

ind.n: Goods description vague or inconsistent across documents
ind.cx: Bill of lading, invoice and letter of credit describe quantity, goods or parties differently.
ind.fp: Clerical errors or HS-code variations occur.
ind.ds: Bill of lading, invoice, customs, letter of credit or payment details disagree on goods, quantity, price, origin, parties or route.
ind.cn: Trade documents inconsistent with each other

ind.n: Multiple invoicing for the same shipment
ind.cx: The same goods are invoiced or financed more than once, or payment references repeat.
ind.fp: Partial shipments and amendments may seem like duplicates.
ind.ds: The same invoice, bill of lading or goods are presented to multiple financiers or invoiced more than once.
ind.cn: Same invoice or shipment financed or invoiced multiple times

ind.n: Shipping route illogical or via high-risk transshipment
ind.cx: Goods travel through jurisdictions with no commercial reason or known risk of trade abuse.
ind.fp: Route changes follow port congestion or carrier network design.
ind.ds: Goods or payments route through third-country hubs or ports with no commercial rationale, or hubs known for rerouting.
ind.cn: Routing through trade-diversion or transshipment hubs

ind.n: Payment from or to unrelated third parties
ind.cx: Payments for goods come from parties not named in the contract or documentation.
ind.fp: Group treasury centres and factoring can legitimately pay.
ind.ds: Funds are paid or received, or instructions are given to pay, through parties with no evident link to the customer, contract, debt or insured interest. Includes third-party cheques, loan repayments, premiums, gaming funds and goods payments not matching the documentation.
ind.cn: Payments from or to unrelated third parties

ind.n: Shipment volume exceeds the counterparty's capability
ind.cx: Quantities or values are out of proportion to the size, history or industry of trading parties.
ind.ds: Quantities or values are out of proportion to the size, history or industry of trading parties.

ind.n: Dual-use or high-risk goods without supporting licences
ind.cx: Trade in goods commonly abused for value transfer (used cars, electronics, gold, scrap) lacks usual licences or logistics.
ind.ds: Trade in goods commonly abused for value transfer (used cars, electronics, gold, scrap) lacks usual licences or logistics.

ind.cx: No verifiable movement of goods: missing tracking, inspection or insurance evidence.
ind.ds: No verifiable movement of goods: missing tracking, inspection or insurance evidence.

ind.n: Frequent amendments or letter of credit changes
ind.cx: Repeated changes to beneficiaries, payment terms or amounts shortly before payment.
ind.ds: Repeated changes to beneficiaries, payment terms or amounts shortly before payment.

ctl.ds: Confirms the existence of underlying goods, services or receivables directly with the obligor or through inspection before funds are advanced. It defeats fictitious invoices and transactions that exist only on paper.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

Reconciles trade documents, invoices and shipments with the payments that settle them and reviews settlement made outside standard banking channels. It exposes trade-based laundering where payment logic does not match the underlying deal.

ctl.n: Duplicate document and duplicate financing detection
ctl.ds: Hashes and fuzzy-matches invoice and shipping documents within and across clients and checks shared registries so one asset cannot be financed twice. It detects reused and fabricated paper.

Applies enhanced checks to operators, counterparties, storage rationale and transactions that involve free-trade zones and free ports, including facility operator controls. It addresses the opacity and reduced oversight these locations can offer.

Compares shipping routes, ports and delivery points with typical lanes and risk lists, and requests explanation for unusual hubs or indirect delivery. It reveals diversion, transshipment and evasion routing.

ctl.n: Counterparty capacity and trade profile assessment
ctl.ds: Tests whether a counterparty's size, history, equipment and sector make the traded volume and goods plausible, and models an expected trade profile to alert on deviation. It detects trading that is out of line with the business.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

Maintains lists of higher-risk goods, species and commodity codes, tags relevant transactions and triggers extra documentary checks and screening of descriptions. It focuses scrutiny on the goods most associated with abuse.

ctl.n: Licence and permit verification for regulated goods
ctl.ds: Validates licences, permits, certificates and authorisations with the issuing authority and compares their scope with observed activity or shipments. It prevents genuine permits being misused or forged permits being accepted.

Verifies that goods physically moved as documented by matching shipping, container, customs and logistics records, and by requesting transport evidence such as delivery confirmations and warehouse records for sampled trades. It exposes fictitious or misdescribed shipments used to justify payments.

Alerts on repeated or late amendments to consignee, destination, price or parties in a trade, and re-runs due diligence on changed parties. It detects manipulation of documents to evade controls after approval.
